articular facet of head of radius: Upper concavity of the radial head; articulates with the capitulum of the humerus.
articular facet of head of stapes: Articular facet of head of stapes
Surface of the head of the stapes that articulates with the incus; stapedius attaches close by.
articular facet of lateral malleolus: Inner surface of the lateral malleolus; takes part in the ankle joint with the talus.
articular facet of medial malleolus: Surface of the medial malleolus that articulates with the talus.
articular facet of tubercle of rib: Articular facet of tubercle of rib
Surface of the tubercle that articulates with the transverse process.
articular facets of head of rib: Articular facets of head of rib
Surfaces of the rib head that articulate with two adjacent vertebral bodies.
articular surface for cuboid: Saddle-shaped articular surface at the front of the calcaneus; forms the calcaneocuboid joint.
articular surface of arytenoid cartilage: Base surface forming the cricoarytenoid joint with the cricoid lamina; opening and closing of the vocal folds takes place at this joint.
articular surface of medial condyle: Oval surface of the medial condyle that articulates with the femur.
articularis genus muscle: Deep fibres of vastus intermedius; during knee extension they pull the suprapatellar bursa upwards so it is not trapped.
ary-epiglottic part of oblique arytenoid: Fibres running in the aryepiglottic fold; they narrow the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.
arytenoid articular surface: Articular surface on the upper border of the cricoid lamina; articulates with the arytenoids.
arytenoid cartilage: Paired pyramid-shaped cartilage on the cricoid lamina; the vocal ligament attaches to its vocal process, and its rotation and gliding open and close the glottis.
ascending part of trapezius muscle: Lower fibres from the lower thoracic spines to the spine of the scapula; depress and upwardly rotate the scapula.
atlas (c1): Ring-shaped first cervical vertebra that carries the skull; it has no body and no spinous process. Its superior articular facets form with the occipital condyles the atlanto-occipital joint, which produces the 'yes' movement.
auricular surface of ilium: Ear-shaped articular surface; forms the sacroiliac joint with the sacrum.
auricular surface of sacrum: Ear-shaped surface forming the sacroiliac joint with the ilium.
axis (c2): The atlas rotates around the dens (odontoid process) projecting up from its body; half of the 'no' movement takes place at the atlanto-axial joint. Dens fractures and the hangman's fracture are typical.
base of arytenoid cartilage: Broad base of the arytenoid; the vocal process projects forwards and the muscular process laterally.
base of coccyx: Upper surface of the coccyx; articulates with the apex of the sacrum.
base of mandible: Lower border of the body of the mandible; the facial artery pulse can be felt here.
base of metatarsal bone: Proximal end of a metatarsal; articulates with the tarsal bones and neighbouring metatarsals.
base of phalanx of foot: Proximal end of a toe phalanx; articulates with the bone before it.
base of phalanx of hand: Proximal end of a finger phalanx; articulates with the metacarpal head or the preceding phalanx.
base of sacrum: Upper surface of the sacrum; articulates with L5 and bears the promontory at its front.
base of stapes: Base of the stapes; it sits in the oval window and transmits vibration to the inner ear.
basilar part of occipital bone: Thick part in front of the foramen magnum (clivus); the brainstem rests on it.
biceps brachii muscle: Inserts into the radial tuberosity and, through the bicipital aponeurosis, into the forearm fascia; a powerful supinator and elbow flexor. Musculocutaneous nerve; biceps reflex C5–C6.
biceps femoris muscle: Lateral hamstring whose long and short heads insert into the fibular head; flexes the knee and rotates the leg laterally when the knee is bent.
bicipitoradial bursa: Between the biceps tendon and the radial tuberosity; reduces friction of the tendon during pronation.
body of clavicle: Body of the clavicle; S-shaped, it most often fractures in its middle third.
body of femur: Shaft of the femur; the linea aspera runs on its posterior surface, and fractures can cause major blood loss.
body of fibula: Thin shaft of the fibula; it does not bear weight but provides attachment for muscles.
body of humerus: Shaft of the humerus; the radial nerve runs in the groove on its posterior surface.
body of hyoid bone: Central body of the hyoid; the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles attach to it.
body of ilium: Body of the ilium contributing to the acetabulum.
body of incus: Body of the incus; articulates with the head of the malleus.
body of ischium: Body of the ischium contributing to the acetabulum.
body of mandible: Horseshoe-shaped body of the mandible; carries the lower teeth.
body of metatarsal bone: Shaft of a metatarsal; stress fractures from walking are most common here.
body of phalanx of hand: Shaft of a finger phalanx; its front surface carries the sheath of the flexor tendons.
body of pubis: Midline body of the pubis; forms the symphysis with the opposite side.
body of radius: Shaft of the radius; it curves slightly outwards, which aids supination.
body of rib: Thin, curved shaft of the rib.
body of sphenoid bone: Cube-shaped body of the sphenoid; it contains the sphenoidal sinus and bears the sella turcica above.
body of sternum: Longest part of the sternum; articulates with the 2nd–7th costal cartilages. Its junction with the manubrium (sternal angle) marks the 2nd rib and the T4–T5 level.
body of talus: Main mass of the talus; the trochlea lies on top of it.
body of tibia: Shaft of the tibia; triangular in cross-section, its anteromedial surface lies just under the skin.
body of ulna: Shaft of the ulna; its posterior border can be felt under the skin.
bones of hand: The 27 bones of the hand: 8 carpal bones, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges.
